title: ReNF: Rethinking the Design of Neural Long-Term Time Series Forecasters

split.decision: ETTh1 standard chronological split: train [0,8640), val [8640,11520), test [11520,14400). All 2785 horizon-96 windows in each evaluation split (test drop_last=False). Full prior history supplied, limit 720 steps enforced by truncation probe; baseline uses 512. No random split.

baseline.paper_ref: Table 1 / Table 6 ETTh1 horizon 96; source main_table/final_1 MSE 0.3508497178554535; manifest 0.35085.
baseline.timing_scope: legacy protocol estimates retained for operational budgeting; not a measured v2 reference

allowed_changes: The entire forecaster, internal feature representation, training surrogate, optimizer, regularizer and training procedure may change within the specified input and data-provenance constraints. The evaluated prediction target and loss formula remain fixed.

When retaining the supplied ReNF training pipeline, changing only learning_rate=0.0006, gamma=0.3, StepLR step_size=2, r_ema=0.996, alpha_freq=0, seq_len=512, d_layers=3, d_ff=2048, batch_size=128, train_epochs=10 or patience=3 does not count as a method improvement.
fixed_contract: Forecast all seven ETTh1 variables for horizon 96 from the allowed history of each window.
The original chronological split, all 2785 evaluation windows, seven channels, horizon 96 and maximum 720-step lookback remain fixed.
Training-standardized multivariate MSE is the fixed objective; MAE remains diagnostic.
Supplied data/splits, evaluation metric, trusted evaluator and lawful information access.
